# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]
- **Documentation**: Phase 02 remediation G hardens the documentation-inventory closure candidate: false one-owner split rows now demote to `unknown-blocking`, dynamic JS/TS consumer parsing skips comments/strings and Markdown prose while retaining fenced code, unresolved alias roots remain standalone gaps, carry-forward refuses pre-existing destinations and refreshes status, and regenerated dynamic fan-out drops from thousands of target items to 128.
- **Documentation**: Phase 02 remediation E hardens documentation-inventory identity and verification: registry lookup keys now exclude classification/status fields, duplicate-title units use semantic fingerprints instead of ordinal anchors, ambiguous duplicate identity emits explicit blockers, dynamic `path.join`/`new URL` consumers emit standalone unresolved patterns, inventory generation requires explicit pinned identity registry input, and checker/verifier enforce registry binding, exact equality, and stale-unit detection.
- **Documentation**: Phase 02 documentation authority unification completed (independent closure-review verdict APPROVE; tagged `documentation-authority-phase-02-20260926`): generated and committed a populated opaque identity registry for all 4,305 immutable-base sources and 85,772 per-occurrence conservation units, then regenerated the deterministic repository-wide inventory + claim-level conservation ledger from immutable base; normal identity misses/ambiguity now become explicit blockers instead of derived fallback IDs; checker/verifier/tests validate registry supply, source coverage, commit-tree digests, shard integrity, owner/claim shape, and exact Phase 02 footprint; blob reads and gate coverage use batched git object reads so the full 4,305-file gate completes in seconds/minutes rather than hanging.
- **Documentation**: Phase 01 documentation authority unification (completed, independent re-review verdict APPROVE, tagged `documentation-authority-phase-01-20260926`): established the operative transitional authority switchboard (docs/transitional-switchboard.md, transitional-switchboard.json) backed by the Phase 00 authority map, published preliminary machine-readable claim-kind and complete §6 source-disposition vocabulary (claim-and-disposition-vocabulary.{json,md}), established deterministic legacy-root file/digest baseline (scripts/check-legacy-docs-ratchet.baseline.json), implemented policy-aware legacy-growth and unaccounted-edit ratchet with strengthened exception lifecycle schema (scripts/check-legacy-docs-ratchet.mjs, scripts/check-legacy-docs-ratchet.exceptions.json, test/scripts/check-legacy-docs-ratchet.test.mjs), codified migration-time one-owner authoring rules (docs/platform/migration-authoring-rules.md), corrected verified stale standing routes in reading maps (replacing defunct fgos-coding-compounding with fgos-coding-knowledge), published deterministic machine-readable inventory of shipped path conventions derived from explicit immutable Git commit tree authority (scripts/generate-shipped-path-inventory.mjs, plans/260925-documentation-authority-unification/shipped-path-conventions-inventory.{json,md}) separating repository-local from consumer-project contracts without filesystem contamination, and codified authoritative verification protocol executing inside an isolated clean detached worktree (scripts/verify-phase-01.mjs) without authorizing Phases 02–09.
- **Documentation**: Phase 00: separated the historical end-user knowledge-registry plan, proposed platform-authority migration, full Knowledge and Documentation Engine horizon, and future Agent Context Engine; added independent review evidence and clarified transitional authority routing (authorizing Phase 01 on isolated cell/branch; Phases 02–09 remain unauthorized).

- Close settled run panes when the gate proves the worker ended and stdout/stderr are captured, including cancellation and non-zero exits; retain crash diagnostics and uncertain attempts. A settlement step that has not completed yet no longer fixes the pane as retained: the pass that completes it decides. `npm run fgos:dev` keeps its staged host while a detached run supervisor still runs from it.

- Reduce dormant Event Store read overhead through validated retained views and current-command Git fact reuse; verify only new active-log tails, preserve append durability, and fix concurrent store benchmark cursors with explicit outside-read timings.

- Keep Event Store retired-path enforcement dormant until the tracked cutover fence; preserve append root durability, tolerate partial maintenance headers, and expose an absent local origin as `null`. Dormant door checks tolerate unrelated Work edits.

- Harden the dormant Event Store: reuse verified reads and stamped Git configuration, avoid syncing untouched directories, expose local maintenance facts and canonical branch keys, and block retired event paths and event-ref bypasses. Store latency benchmarks can seed realistic history without a Work consumer.

- `fgos worktree create` now provisions the new checkout after the Git port returns: dependency install, then the project's `worktreeSetup.commands`. This repo's setup also copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout, so a worker in that worktree can use `ak:cook`. The setup no longer builds the Rust workspace in each new worktree (a run that needs a binary builds it with its own Cargo target). `fgos setup` no longer deletes skills other tools installed into `.agents/skills` (only entries fgOS itself assembled are pruned). The claude executor declares `ak:cook` in `supports.skills`, and `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill is missing from the runtime's skill directory. `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md` is the brief for an `ak:cook` worker.
- Add the `debate` collaboration pattern: a thesis side and an antithesis side argue blind in parallel, answer each other's round-1 argument (`params.rebuttal: false` skips it), and a read-only judge on a provider family different from both sides rules; a pool that cannot seat such a judge is refused by name. `group-cognition`'s dialectical step now runs `debate` instead of `reviewed`, and its action synthesis builds on the judge's ruling.

- Add `fgos worktree remove <path> --delivered-to <ref>`: removes a worktree through the Worktree port, which refuses a dirty checkout, one a process stands in, preserved worker state, or a tip not contained in the delivery target (branch name, full ref or object id). No force flag; the delivery statement is recorded as the operation's evidence digest.

- Git typed commit and recovery reads ignore user signature/display settings; suite subprocess census no longer requires strace.

- Git typed operations batch storage and commit-header reads, reuse operation-local checkout facts and index evidence, and expose paired per-phase Git/holder-lock census diagnostics.

- Git hooks ownership excludes included config files; interrupted native-lock exchanges resume automatically using the recorded guard identity. GitHub merge diagnostics retain pre-connect failures and stop polling terminal PRs, and restore extraction preserves missing worktree registrations as exclusions.

- Git recovery preserves live Publication and non-event transfer lock contracts, releases terminal ref pins, tolerates prunable extraction registrations, and atomically guards Linux native-lock quarantine; GitHub merge timeouts query server state before a later request.

- Git deadline cleanup now gives children three seconds to terminate cooperatively; unowned native index locks refuse with `native-index-lock-unowned` and a read-only holder report plus the retained-lock runbook.

- Git Recovery reconciles ConfigChange under repo-config authority; hooks configuration preserves inherited values and removes only owned local settings. Native quarantine detects inode substitution after rename.

- SafeRestore extraction refuses sibling worktrees and the state root, binds creation to a directory descriptor, and recognizes tracked case-only aliases. Add a dormant partial Recovery facade, a GitHub timeout/query contract test, and paired typed-operation E3 budget rows.

- Git adds dormant native index-lock inspection/quarantine and owned hooks configuration APIs, with exact inode/value guards and WAL recovery; existing setup and mutation callers remain on their current paths.

- Git Land can recover an observed candidate after later destination commits without touching checkout/index; unrelated main merge/bisect state no longer blocks prepare/publish or terminal receipt replay.

- SafeRestore refuses untracked/ignored collisions unless exact replacement paths are authorized, captures only local bytes, preserves incoming executable modes and intent-to-add, and exposes snapshot extraction and acknowledgement-gated cleanup. Unreadable snapshots no longer permanently block a checkout.

- Git Land recovery blocks unreconciled predecessor effects, tolerates index stat refresh, preserves ignored store collisions and permits acknowledged cleanup of abandoned/lost candidates.

- Add dormant SafeRestore preview/apply/recover ports with durable binary/index/untracked/mode snapshots, verified checkout custody, local delta reapplication and observe-only crash recovery.

- Git Land preserves unrelated staged changes, closes abandoned prepares at admission, and reports attempted retries and CAS failures consistently with recovery.

- Add dormant Land recovery through the existing Rust/addon/Node port, observe-only CAS recovery, recorded checkout fingerprints, acknowledgement-gated cleanup and compacted receipt replay.

- Add dormant Git Land prepare/publish ports with immutable candidates, consumer verification binding, own-file checkout protection, one-shot CAS and operation-id receipt replay; production callers remain unchanged.

- The coordination driver doctrine (`core/skills/_shared/coordination-driver.md`, loaded by `fgos-advise` and the other coordination facades) now teaches the case model: observe with `fgos workflow status <caseId>`, choose an activity and route yourself, dispatch with `--case` and `--activity` on every run (read-only included), treat a refusal as an answer, ask a person only for the listed triggers, close with `fgos workflow close`. It no longer tells a driver to run `fgos workflow operations` on a run.

- Provider accounts of one pool are now taken in the order the config declares them, no longer by fewest leases or oldest use: the first account takes every lease until it is quarantined or disabled, then the next. A pool declared in `runner.llmAccounts` now supplies its own accounts to the lease (a `codex` store as a Codex home, any other store with the login files its invocations declare); a pool it does not declare keeps reading `runner.providers`. An account id of digits only is refused, since such a key would sort ahead of the others. `runner.tierFallback` (tier to ordered list of families) is checked by the new doctor row `tier-fallback`.

- A seat that fails on a provider limit or a dead login now walks the tier it runs at: first the remaining models of its family's cell for that tier (each `model@pool` entry is served by its own pool and its own accounts), then the families `runner.tierFallback.<tier>` lists, limited to the families the capability's `prefer` names and never leaving the tier. A pool no enabled account of can run (no account holding the CLI's login store) is not a candidate, and a dead login excludes that pool only, not the family's other pools. The leading family of a seat still follows `prefer`. `fgos run --account` and `fgos workflow start --account` now take `pool/account` (for example `openai/work`); a bare account id is refused with the form to write. A tier with no model for an out-of-process agent seat's family now refuses with `tier-cell-missing`, naming `runner.modelPolicies.<family>.<tier>`; `executor.model` and the `default` model no longer stand in for a missing cell. `fgos dispatch explain` prints the candidates in order (with why one is out), the walk, and the accounts of each pool on it in lease order. A unit record written before this change restarts its walk at the primary.

- `fgos doctor` row `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` now recomputes a fallback attempt with the seat's earlier bindings, the way the write gate does, so it no longer reports a binding mismatch for every attempt after the first; a binding that differs from its walk still fails. The messages of `model-policy-pools` and `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` now say that the walk skips a pool with no usable account and that the lease reads `runner.llmAccounts` for a pool it declares.
- Git checkout operations revalidate config file stamps before each child and refuse post-hook promisor changes while retaining the reduced preflight exec count.

- Git: reuse config and storage-format checks within each ScopedCommit/Sync call, recheck after hooks, and retain per-child topology and custody validation.
- A Unit that writes is no longer run without asking whether a Workflow case owns its worktree. `runUnit` takes the admission port from its caller (the Execution Core owns the interface, the Workflow implements it, every entry point injects it): a writing Unit without the port is refused as `case-admission-port-missing`, a standalone writing run goes on only into a worktree no case binds, and a Unit that names a case is admitted before custody and the unit directory, linked in `unit.json` as `{ caseId, activity, reservationId }` (older records still read), held to a seat-launch ceiling (planned seats times the frame's fallback allowance; a provider limit keeps `fallbackExhausted`, a reviewed run that cannot start its next round ends at its last evaluation), rechecked at the write gate (`consent-stale` commits nothing) and settled once. The Playbook proposer, `fgos run`, the Work dispatch, operation-choice and fan-out paths all inject the real port; the Work paths get `unbound` and behave as before.

- `fgos run --case <id> --activity <id> [--route should|may-instead|unlisted] [--reason <text>]` and `fgos workflow start --case <parentId>` name the case a run belongs to. Every signal a call gives (the reference, the case variables its door set, the binding of the worktree it writes) must name one open case: `authority-context-conflict` and `authority-context-invalid` (unknown, malformed, closed: never standalone), `bound-worktree-requires-case-authority` for a writing run into a bound worktree that names no case, `playbook-case-admits-via-proposer-only` for a call from outside a Playbook case's proposer, and `nested-write-from-confined-worker` for a writing dispatch from inside a confined worker. Workers no longer inherit `FGOS_CASE_ID`/`FGOS_CASE_RESERVATION`: the door sets them from the reservation it admitted (codex gets them beside its writer id in injected config). A nested case or `--units` wave is charged to its parent's frame first and given back, exactly once, when it cannot open.

- A Playbook case that ran to a pass now closes itself, by the same rules as `fgos workflow close` (quiet bindings released); a failed, blocked or parked case stays open for `resume` and `answer`, and a conductor case still closes only through `fgos workflow close`.

- A gate approval can be given again for content that changed after it was approved. The digest of an edited report is now the digest of the bytes that lie there (it used to become unknown), so the gate asks again, the re-approval is bound to the new digest, and the next Unit is handed the revision a person approved instead of being refused as `report-changed-after-settle`; an edit no approval covers is still refused.

- `fgos doctor` row `git-worktree-recovery` no longer fails on a worktree whose `git worktree lock` reason names a process that is still running (pid and start time checked, a reused pid does not count); a lock naming a dead or unparseable owner stays a finding.

- Event Store migration refuses published mirror conflicts before changing the local legacy ref, restores pre-commit filesystem failures, and computes dry-run identities through Rust and the read-only Git port.

- Fix dormant Event Store migration retries and recovery ownership, pre-cutover doctor warnings, HEAD-only reads, and restorable nested porting rollback exports.

- Add dormant Event Store migration/import and rollback parity support, HEAD-only legacy reads, migration-required write refusals, and legacy-layout diagnostics; CLI registration follows at cutover.

- `fgos workflow` plays by the case model. The playbook runner is now the Playbook proposer: it asks admission for every Unit (entry milestones, consent bound to the approved artifact, independent seats, disjoint writes, worktree binding, the approved frame), records a route and a reservation before the Unit runs and a settle with its receipts after, and parks the gate again when an approval no longer matches the artifact it approved; the order the playbooks run in does not change. `workflow answer` keeps the answer as a file and, while a proposer is alive, leaves it to record the answer before it acts (nothing else is started); `status` adds a `case` block (milestones with digests, listed routes and the unlisted path, frame left, open gates, live reservations); new `fgos workflow close <id>` (refused while a closure milestone is stale or a consent gate is parked); `start` takes `--frame key=value,...` to narrow the guide's frame, never widen it. A guide with its own activities opens a conductor case: a case id and no driving process. `src/workflow/runner.mjs` is split by role into `unit-handoff`, `case-lock`, `case-start`, `case-verbs`, with the proposer loop left in `runner.mjs`.
- A Workflow case now has a model behind its ledger: milestones bound to the digest of their subject, reservations, the approved frame with its counters, routes and deviations, receipts from named evaluators only, and an admission check that answers whether a proposed activity may run now (entry milestones, consent bound to the approved artifact, independent seats, disjoint write scopes, binding, frame). A worktree is bound to one case through one record file per worktree identity. A gate answer is now one file per round that is never rewritten, and a second answer to an answered gate is refused (`gate-already-answered`). `fgos doctor` gains `workflow-case-binding-sentinel` and `workflow-case-bindings` (and `--fix` for the latter).
- Git: defer foreign-checkout cleanup failures after durable closure, preserve Sync receipt replay across branch changes, name detached-HEAD refusal, and document reflog-only recovery.

- Restore WAL exclusion between checkout and worktree lifecycle operations; refuse reflog-only commit attribution, bind Sync recovery to its recorded branch, close foreign attempted chains honestly, and retain sync warnings in runner results.

- Bind checkout WAL to directory identity, recover hook-modified and reflog-visible commits, preserve terminal causes and landed receipts across compaction failures, protect async siblings during native Git loans, and retain clean-file permissions during rollback. Add an aged-floor Node-loan E3 row for host acceptance.

- Git: recover interrupted scoped commits without replay, unblock pre-attempt/rejected Sync transactions, bound terminal WAL history, preserve concurrent sibling borrows, and restore clean merge paths on abort. E3 now measures Node-loaned checkout custody.

- Restore declared producer bytes, modes and move paths after rejecting ScopedCommit hooks; drain adopted setsid lock borrowers without harming unrelated pre-exec children.

- Preserve acquisition reach provenance in native holder-lock handover and emit Git WAL addon capabilities from the shared release/dev/test producer. Prevent uncertain Sync commit retries after a controller crash and preserve actual hook-modified file sets on receipt replay. Phase 05 remains unreleased pending its remaining acceptance proofs.

- Add dormant native ScopedCommit, Sync and non-event Checkpoint ports, a Rust write-scope leaf, and an activated-host cutover grant check. Linux-x64 activation refuses a missing addon or missing `git-wal-v1` addon capability. Production adapter migration remains phase 07.

- Workflow definitions load into one guide model (milestones, activities, decision points, MUST rows that each name an existing check, unenforced rules, frame defaults). Playbooks keep their steps and gain a short guide head; a MUST naming a check outside the catalog, an expression field, `listedRoutesOnly` outside a decision point, or `rigorCeiling` is a load error. A run's start event records the normalised guide.

- `fgos workflow start --plan` is removed (an unknown flag now): the AgentKit plan is read as an artifact and its phases run as Units through `fgos run` or `fgos workflow start --units <file>`. The coding workflow file drops its dead runner fields (`units`, `dependsOn`, `gate` and the `integrate` and `approval` steps); its lifecycle part is unchanged.
- End terminal rounds with `terminal:result-unreadable` when an invalid result stays unchanged for 30 seconds and the agent is idle, releasing custody through normal settlement.
- Preserve committed decision-index rows missing from local state during setup and doctor fixes; exclude git-ignored setup output consistently from release payloads and checkout drift checks.
- Warn once per unreadable pid per Worktree removal or relocation, and allow clean tracked `.fgos` while preserving reappearing skip-worktree state and dirty bytes.
- Arm the Linux terminal gate’s parent-death signal so a killed sandbox monitor ends its namespace; read all kernel lock-table pages while retaining shared-probe release confirmation.

- Warn with pid and comm when a same-user process cwd is unreadable during Worktree removal or relocation; readable checkout cwds still refuse.

- Fix Worktree allocation under `.claude/worktrees`, multi-user cwd checks and terminal recovery of clean Git refusals; require reachable delivery before removal and report preserved dirty checkouts as advisory diagnostics.

- Add `fgos worktree create <path> [--branch <name> | --detach] [--base <ref>]`: serialized worker checkout creation with stripped `.fgos`, plus read-only `git-worktree-recovery` diagnostics. Dormant native Worktree removal, relocation and evidence-bound crash recovery preserve dirty or uncertain checkouts.
- Ctrl-C and SIGTERM of `fgos run` now stop the run cleanly: no commit, reviewer, verify or next round starts after the signal, a signal during the hand-over of an attempt cancels it once it binds, and the resume line is always printed. A malformed `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` or `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` is a named validation error, and `fgos doctor` names an attempt whose release was removed and how to recover it. Library callers of the runner keep their own signal handling.

- Fix custody admission for busy worktrees, preserve settled results on handoff errors, distinguish reused cwd inodes, and restore 64 MiB commit output capture with overflow errors on every platform.

- Writing Unit runs retain cwd custody through runner commits and lend it to git/hooks and to the Unit verify command; successor admission preserves unprovable predecessor worktrees. Mutating producers require a supervised domain, and `--force-shared-cwd` with writes is refused. Workflow redispatches an unknown custody predecessor in a fresh worktree while preserving its old checkout and branch. Custody refusals include cwd, executor and capability context.

- Preserve historical Publication transfer WAL digests; classify transport config by Git scope across linked worktrees and symlinked paths. Doctor now explains refused repo-local CI credentials: use actions/checkout `persist-credentials: false` with a trusted global credential helper or `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`-level setting.

- Harden Git Remote against repository URL/transport redirects; make pushes atomic, settle forced remote-tracking fetches with exact-old checks, and tighten checkout and branch-use preflight with one shared transfer WAL shape.

- Git adds dormant typed Refs and non-event Remote facades: checked-out branches are protected under worktree-admin, fast-forward checkout updates require custody, transfers use explicit mappings and preserve unknown outcomes without resending. Opaque one-shot native lock handover blocks release during calls and rejects forged handles; Windows handover remains unsupported.

- Git adds a dormant typed Inspect facade with byte-safe status/diff/object/path/worktree reads, explicit trunk uncertainty and shallow ancestry errors, bounded streamed write snapshots on Unix, and transaction-local Rust lock scopes seeded only by verified holder handles. Diff hardening flags now precede the path delimiter. Linked-worktree cwd discovery validates reciprocal main registration; separate-git-dir remains unsupported.
- Bind Event Store appends to prepared machine authority, remove raw store construction, require trusted-main preparation, and tighten gate/error/consumer validation.

- Harden Git landing repairs: ignore reserved legacy mirror suffixes, diagnose their refs, migrate historical origin mappings alongside custom remotes, preserve symlinked state roots, and refuse unrelated-root chmod with actionable hooks diagnostics.

- Fix Git setup so ordinary fetch/pull work before the legacy Event Store ref exists; repair previously installed exact refspecs, share Git’s mapping policy across setup and Event Store, and repair/diagnose unsafe Git driver directory modes on umask-002 hosts.

- Git rollback WAL scans ignore durable-file temporaries in the compaction ledger using the same rule as other WAL readers; incomplete or corrupt installed entries still refuse.
- Git Publication now checks changing candidates through the successful connectivity fast path, makes replayed Intent directories durable, preserves full recoverable receipts through compaction, and tolerates scans racing terminal compaction. Recreated loose objects get fresh directory durability; deferred compaction failures are reported.
- The optional `git-floor-verdict.json` cache binds Git/config/PATH and host/probe identities and requires the exact probe set; include directives disable persistent reuse. Holder-lock uses one lagged scan for borrow cleanup and quiescent admission, then settles exclusive Linux release (including dropped guards) using positive kernel-table evidence plus an inode-checked shared probe (brief Try contention), killing escaped descriptor recipients at release; Publication close returns the cleanup outcome. Holder-lock also fixes its Windows time imports. Mapped process spawning resolves relative PATH entries in the child directory and runs executable scripts without a shebang.
- A confined invocation can declare the login store it reads with `credentialStore` (`use`, `homeEnv`, optional `files`) in the runner config; the sandbox points that variable at its private home and copies the store's files, and an invocation that declares none gets no login. Files of the store that are absent are now skipped instead of refusing the launch; a store with none present still refuses, with a named reason. `fgos dispatch explain` shows the store of the bound invocation, and `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` covers every confined invocation that reads a store. Older configs that bind `private-home` to an env variable keep working. This repo's own config now declares stores, drops the account name from invocation ids (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`, `pi-cli-bwrap`) and no longer carries the OpenRouter key variable for pi.
- Codex terminal runs deliver the brief through the terminal-control prompt door instead of typing it and pressing Enter, so a long brief is no longer left unsubmitted in the composer; the paste-chip matcher also recognizes codex's `[Pasted Content N chars]`.
- Releases ship a combined Git/Event Store Node addon through optional `components.nativeAddon`; its manifest attests build inputs without binding future upgrades to the verifier's Cargo.lock. Only Linux advertises `git-wal-v1` while C5 scan/fence support is Linux-only; Windows activation remains available and lock-taking Git ports refuse with `git-lockscope-unavailable-windows`.
- Config mapping failures resolve their WAL chain and remove only their own native staging lock. Re-running activation installs a missing Git fence; WAL writers refuse an unfenced workspace. Older `fgctl` stops with `EISDIR` at the fenced legacy activation lock. Channels without the optional addon report informational Git checks until M10.

- Git doctor now checks the combined addon ABI and Git floor, repository topology, WAL backlog/retained bytes, native lock residue, publication fetch mappings and durability limits (`git-component-compatible`, `git-trust-topology`, `git-operation-journal`, `git-native-locks`, `git-publication-refspecs`, `git-durability-capability`). Registered setup fixes initialize the WAL and, on `fgos setup`, install the additive origin mirror mappings `+refs/fgos/events/*:refs/fgos/remotes/origin/events/*` and `+refs/fgos/legacy:refs/fgos/remotes/origin/legacy` through the Rust config writer.

- Git WAL admission in `fgctl` uses `activation-v2.lock` and fences old controllers at first WAL-capable activation. Pending operations block rollback to a release without `git-wal-v1`; corrupt or incomplete WAL scans refuse activation. Atomic fence placement currently requires Linux.
- The Rust Git component can install additive Event Store fetch mappings under `repo-config` 80, preserving user settings and recording the effective remote URL in WAL provenance. The combined Node binding and doctor/setup integration are registered.
- Event Store sync authenticates its own reconciliation merges (the exact verified prior tip and candidate are authorized before the ref CAS), verifies each mirror independently so a rewound or forged foreign mirror becomes a typed warning instead of blocking own publication, and reports every tracked-fence mismatch as `event-store-legacy-mismatch`. Re-running fetch-mapping setup when mappings already exist records an effect-free `configApproved` WAL outcome.

### Added
- `fgos run "<prompt>" --input <a>,<b> --verify "<cmd>"` hands the Unit its input files and the command that checks its work; both are Unit fields (`inputs`, `verify`) that units files and workflow templates carry too, and a Unit may also name `skills`, which only executors declaring them in `supports.skills` can serve (refusal reason `skills-unavailable`).
- `docs:write` is a curated capability slot that `fgos setup` declares next to `code:implement`.
- Ctrl-C (or SIGTERM) on `fgos run` stops the attempts it handed over by name: the controller asks each supervisor to cancel, waits for the receipts for at most `dispatch.cancelWaitMs`, prints `unit <id> chờ resume: fgos run --resume <id>` and exits 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM); a second signal exits at once and the attempts still end `cancelled`. Config key `dispatch.cancelWaitMs` (default `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` + 5000, at least 1000), read by the same project-over-global reader as the kill grace; `fgos setup` does not write it.
- `fgos dispatch inspect`, `dispatch show-run` and `fgos run --json` report `attemptState` and `unitState`; a unit whose controller is gone and whose last attempt is closed reads `awaiting-resume` and names `fgos run --resume <unit>`.
- `fgos dispatch recover` over an attempt of the run supervisor recommends `adopt`.
- `fgos doctor` checks `legacy-attempts-stuck` (runs from before the run supervisor still `running`; `--fix` settles them as `abandoned-legacy` only when every process they recorded is dead and no version-1 home is left, and names the reason for each run it keeps), `units-awaiting-resume` (lists the units to resume, never fails) and `cancel-wait` (`dispatch.cancelWaitMs` and its source; fails below 1000 ms or below `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs`).
- Terminal-control lays panes out from the real size of the tab (`measured-split`): it splits the pane whose smaller half stays largest, and opens a new tab of the same group when no split keeps a pane of at least `terminal.layout.minCols` x `minRows` or the tab holds `maxPanesPerTab`.
- Config section `terminal` (setup adds it when missing): `allocationGraceMs` (60000, the ready timeout plus 30 s at least), `retainFailedPaneMs` (`null`: keep a failed pane until a person closes it), `layout.policy` (`measured-split`), `layout.minCols` (80), `layout.minRows` (20), `layout.maxPanesPerTab` (8). Project over global over default. `fgos setup` also creates `<stateRoot>/terminal` (mode 0700). No new environment variable.
- `fgos doctor` checks `terminal-control` (driver, declared capabilities and herdr server incarnation; a missing herdr is a warning and says direct mode is unaffected; a bad `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` fails), `terminal-config` (each `terminal.*` value with its source; fails by name on a rule it breaks) and `terminal-allocations` (slots stuck past the grace and retained panes past their time; reports only, closes nothing).
- `herdr-spawn` rounds, the account probe and the confinement reaper now reach herdr only through terminal-control. Panes of one batch (a coding panel, or the attempts of one unit run) share one tab labeled with the batch key, and the first worker's own pane opens the tab, so no empty root pane is left and fgOS never closes a tab. A pane kept for a person after a failed round stays open and can be closed by its slot key (`terminalKey` in `visibility.json`); a confined home written by an older release names no slot, so its pane is not closed on a guess. The `fgos-lead-<key>-<ts>` tab labels are gone. Needs a host with the `fgos internal terminal-control` route (an activated release built from this source, or `FGOS_HOST_BIN`).
- Windows now has a holder-lock driver (`LockFileEx` in the locking process; Node holds a lock through one `fgos internal lock-hold` helper per lock). The gateway, sessions, runner, dispatch, advance, recovery, the provider locks, `fgctl` activation and observe all take their kernel locks on Windows, so `fgos run` no longer refuses there with `lock-driver-unavailable`. A git child that borrows a lock runs in a named job that ends with the borrow. `fgos doctor` reports `lockfileex`/`kernel`, and the borrow vectors and the `fgctl` activation gate run on Windows. A crash during a borrowed git commit costs about 120-170 ms at the next acquire. A `windows-job` predecessor record is judged by the host (`fgos internal lock-fd --predecessor-state`, read-only), and `lock-holders` warns with the domain and the reason when it is not empty.
- `fgos dispatch explain --for <capability> [--rigor <r>]` shows why a capability runs where it does, without running anything: the family and the `prefer` entry that chose it, the tier and where it came from (rigor, override, `maxTier`), the whole `modelPolicies` cell with the entry that runs, the executor and invocation, and the accounts of the family's pool in `runner.providers` and `runner.llmAccounts`.
- `fgos doctor` checks for the model, pool and account config: `executor-family-unique` (two agent executors of one family fail), `model-policy-pools` (a `model@pool` cell entry whose pool `runner.llmAccounts` does not declare warns), `llm-accounts-shape` (a malformed `runner.llmAccounts`, or one in the project config, fails), `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` (once `runner.llmAccounts` is declared, accounts or login directories that differ from `runner.providers` warn; the lease still reads `runner.providers`) and `global-model-policies-portable` (a list or `model@pool` cell in `~/.fgos/config.json` fails).
- A `runner.modelPolicies.<family>.<tier>` cell in the project config may name the pool that serves the model (`model@pool`, split at the last `@`) or list several in order (`["deepseek-v4@openrouter", "deepseek-v4"]`). A run uses the first entry served by the family's own pool (an entry without `@`); entries for other pools are accepted and wait for pool routing. The global `~/.fgos/config.json` keeps plain strings only: a list or `@` cell there is ignored with a warning, because older fgOS releases on the machine cannot read it. A cell with no entry for the family's pool counts as a missing tier.
- `fgos doctor` checks for holder-lock, the kernel locks behind gateway, sessions, runner, dispatch and the provider accounts: `lock-kernel-semantics` (both lock directories give kernel exclusion, proven by a two-process probe; a network filesystem and a platform with no lock driver fail by name; on Windows it reports `lockfileex`/`kernel`), `lock-borrow-vectors` (a lock lent to a git child never leaks to a background process; red fails), `lock-holders` (warns on a holder that is not a fgOS process, and on a previous holder's processes still running), `lock-fences` (warns while a legacy lock path has no cutover fence), `lock-predecessor-kill-wait` and `state-root` (Node and the host resolve the same state root).
- `fgos doctor` check `lock-record-unreadable` warns when the `state` or `porting-events` hot record in `.fgos/locks/` does not parse, or names a holder the judge cannot place for more than five minutes; it names the file and `fgos lock fence <name>`, and never fixes by itself.
- On Windows the `state` and `porting-events` hot locks now reclaim a crashed holder like on Linux: the holder's creation time is read through the new host route `fgos internal process-observe`, so a dead holder's record is cleaned within the five second wait and a live one never is; an unopenable holder or a host that cannot be run still fails closed (`fgos lock fence`).
- On Windows a borrowed git child and the job keeper no longer inherit the handles the lock holder owns: they are started with an explicit inherited-handle list holding only their own standard streams.
- Config key `lock.predecessorKillWaitMs` (default 2000 ms, 1 to 60000): the longest wait, after the processes a dead lock holder left are killed, for them to exit before the lock goes to the next holder. `fgos setup` adds it and creates `.fgos/locks` and `~/.local/state/fgos/locks` (mode 0700).
- `fgos doctor --fix` (and `fgos setup`) places the cutover fences once the workspace's activated release runs holder-lock and no other fgOS process of the workspace is running; it lists the processes still running instead of placing anything. Activate this release in every workspace first, then fence.
- `fgctl` refuses to activate a release when the holder-lock semantics probe or the borrow vectors are red on this machine (`lock-kernel-semantics-failed`, `lock-borrow-vectors-failed`); the gate runs on Windows too, and a platform with no lock driver refuses with `lock-kernel-semantics-failed`.
- New skill `instruction-audit` (`/instruction-audit`) audits any repository's agent instruction surface on demand or on a schedule. It measures what each agent runtime (Claude Code, AGENTS.md readers, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot) loads on every turn, finds blocks loaded twice and which tool wrote them, duplicate or broken hook registrations, and paths in settings that no longer exist. It also runs read-only lanes over rules, enforcement and git history, and writes a ranked report with a delta against the previous run. It never edits the files it audits.
- `fgos identity [--pid <n>] [--fgos-dir <dir>]` prints which writer the calling process is, as `{id, source}`. The answer comes from one place, the Rust crate `fgos-session-identity`, which Node now calls for every state write; `fgos doctor` check `writer-identity-resolvable` asks both the running host and the activated release (the one a plain `git commit` hook uses).
- `fgos workflow start` supports `--timeout <dur>` and `--account <id>` flags, propagating overrides down to each Unit run while honoring Unit self-declared timeouts.
- `fgos doctor` check `executor-posture-coverage` verifies that core capabilities have executors capable of applying required posture, providing actionable remediation instructions when misconfigured.
- `fgos run --timeout <dur>` (for example `90m` or `5400s`, from 1m to 4h), a `"timeoutMs"` key in `--override`, or a Unit's own `timeoutMs` (also in a units file) gives one run more (or less) time than `runner.timeoutMs`. The value is kept for resume (`--timeout` is refused with `--resume`). A run longer than an hour no longer has its private home reclaimed mid-turn, and a dispatch with a shorter timeout no longer takes the worktree lock of a longer run. `runner.timeoutMs` above 4h is now refused.
- `fgos run --sync <ref>` (Unit field `syncBase`) merges a branch into the worktree's branch before the worker runs: the runner runs the merge and commits it, so a confined worker never needs git. A clean merge is committed as `chore(sync): merge <ref>`; on conflicts the conflicted files join the write scope and the worker's brief, and the runner concludes the merge commit after a passing round, refusing while a conflict marker is left (`fgos run --resume` then commits once they are gone). `--sync <ref> --writes <paths>` without a prompt only syncs. A sync never takes the base's changes under `.fgos/` (the branch keeps its own), and a pre-commit hook that refuses the merge commit is reported as `hook-refused` with the hook's message.
- `fgos doctor`'s `workflow-capabilities-configured` also warns when `code:implement`, the capability the runner loop's coding executing step asks for, has no `prefer` pool.
- `fgos run --effort low|medium|high|max` (or `"reasoningEffort"` in `--override`) sets how hard the worker reasons for one run, without editing the provider's own config. claude and agy get `--effort`, pi and omp `--thinking`, Codex `-c model_reasoning_effort=` (`max` becomes `xhigh`). A level outside that list, or one the bound executor's `supports.reasoningEffort` does not declare, is refused before the worker starts (`fgos run` reports a `policy-refusal` with reason `reasoning-effort`). Until now a derived effort was recorded in the policy but never reached the CLI; that is unchanged when no effort is given.
- A run's result records where the model that ran differs from the one bound, under `policy.provenance.modelDrift`: replaced by policy before launch (`model-overridden`), not passed on the command line (`model-not-passed`), refused or unknown to the provider CLI (`model-unsupported`), or reported differently by the CLI (`model-reported-different`).
- `fgos run "<prompt>"` runs a one-line task as a Unit. The flags are `--provider` (soft preference), `--persona`, `--writes` (needs a linked worktree), `--capability` (default `execute`), `--rigor`, `--effort` and `--override`. Without `--writes` the Unit is read-only. A wrong provider, a wrong persona, or writes from the main checkout fail before anything runs.
- `fgos workflow start --units <file>` (a YAML/JSON list of Units) runs the list as a one-off Workflow, one step per Unit. A Unit may carry `prefer` (soft preference) and `persona`; `--units` does not combine with `--seats`.
- `fgos workflow start --effort <level>` asks the same reasoning effort for every unit of the run, kept across resume.
- A Unit may declare `prefer` (a soft executor preference) and `persona`. Its `prefer` goes ahead of the capability's pool, passing the same filters and failing over into the pool; its `persona` binds unless an override names one. Binding provenance records `unit-prefer` / `unit` as the source.
- `fgos run --resume` after a failed runner commit only commits again; the agent does not run a second time. A stray commit holding files outside the write scope blocks the resume until it is taken off the branch (`git reset HEAD~1`).
- Config key `runner.generatedPaths` and doctor check `runner-generated-paths`: a Unit that edits a generated source (for example `core/skills/**`) gets the rendered copies in its write scope too.
- `agent-result.json` takes an optional `needsWrites`: paths the worker needed outside its write scope and did not write.
- `fgos run --account <id>` (or `"account"` in `--override`) pins the provider account: each seat whose bound executor's provider lists that account runs on it, through the normal lease. A pin no seat can take, or an account that is quarantined (the message says until when), is refused before anything runs, and a resume is refused while the pinned account is quarantined. A provider limit on a pinned account ends the seat instead of switching account or executor. Pair it with `--provider` to choose the executor.
- A writing seat that already changed the worktree when it hit a provider limit is no longer run again on another account or executor on top of that half-done work: the unit stops as `provider-limit` with `fallbackExhausted.reason: "partial-writes"` and the changed paths. Read-only seats, and seats that changed nothing, rotate as before.
- `fgos --help --json` and `fgos <verb> [<sub>] --help --json` work through the installed `fgos` in any project: `--help` and `-h` are routed to the verb manifest, `<verb> <sub> --help --json` narrows to one sub-verb, and a Rust-native verb (`version`, `metrics`, `friction`, `convention`, `gate-bypass`) given `--help` prints its manifest entry instead of running. Verbs with sub-verbs (`dispatch`, `workflow`, `merge`, `session`, `gateway`, `goal`, `tool`, `agents`, `metrics`, `friction`, `convention`) list each sub-verb's flags, required fields and examples under `subcommands`.
- `fgctl upgrade` resolves its target release by `--from <path | URL>` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION=<tag>` > the latest GitHub release, verifies a downloaded archive against `SHA256SUMS` before staging, and records the downloaded tag in `.fgos/distribution.json` (`projectRuntime.releaseVersion`) so teammates can acquire the upgraded release via plain `fgctl init`.
- `fgos run` direct attempts are owned by a Rust run supervisor and a gate that is pid 1 of the attempt's process domain (Linux: bwrap PID namespace, or a process group where user namespaces are off; Windows: a Job Object; macOS: a process group tree, best-effort). A controller that dies or is killed no longer loses the CLI's result: the agent keeps running to its deadline, the receipt is written, and the next `fgos run`, runner loop, `dispatch` or `fgos doctor --fix` settles the attempt through `fgos internal adopt`. A supervisor that never started (on Windows, an attempt lock it could not take) is reported with its reason (`start-refused:lock-held`), not only in `supervisor.log`.
- `fgos doctor` checks for the run supervisor: `process-containment` (the driver agents run in and its level, `kernel` or `best-effort`, with the routes around it; a Linux machine with no user namespace warns and never fails), `run-supervisor-route` (the host serves `supervise`, `gate`, `adopt` and `attempt-step` at protocol 1), `runtime-socket-dir` (exists, 0700, yours; setup and `--fix` create it), `run-attempts-stuck` (an attempt with no holder and no `closed.json`; `--fix` adopts it) and `gate-kill-grace`. `lock-holders` counts a bwrap monitor under an attempt's supervisor as a member of the attempt.
- A herdr round now survives the death of the process that started it. The run supervisor watches the pane (deadline, idle, cancel, the pane itself), types the brief, reads the result, settles, and closes the pane for a clean end; a controller that is killed, a supervisor that is killed after the brief (the agent runs on and its result is still settled) and a pane that disappears (the attempt ends as `carrier-lost`) each end with a named outcome and no pane left behind. A pane that stops answering is blind time, never idle time. A finished attempt closes its pane once; any other end keeps it (24 hours by default, `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs`).
- A worker started by `fgos run` now writes under its own writer id, `att-<attemptId>`, in a pane and headless alike: `FGOS_SESSION_ID` is that id, the controller's `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID` and parent `FGOS_PARENT_WRITER_ID` never reach the worker, and `FGOS_PARENT_WRITER_ID` names the controller's writer id. A command run by codex under its shared daemon sees the attempt id only because the codex launch now carries `-c shell_environment_policy.set={FGOS_SESSION_ID="..."}`.
- `fgos doctor` check `runtime-socket-dir` also reports attempt sockets that no supervisor holds any more (a supervisor killed before it could remove its socket); `fgos doctor --fix` removes only those socket files. `run-attempts-stuck` covers panes as well as headless attempts.
- Config key `dispatch.gateKillGraceMs` (default 10000 ms, at least 1000): the wait between SIGTERM and SIGKILL when the gate stops an agent. Project config overrides global; `fgos setup` does not write it.

### Changed
- A reviewed run's verify step now runs the Unit's own `verify` (or its capability's) through the bounded command runner, for at most `runner.timeoutMs`, and a failure or a timeout becomes findings that say which; the `code-change` preset no longer pins `npm test` (it was never executed), and a reviewed run with no verify command reports `verify: { ran: false }` in its result instead of passing silently.
- At rigor `high` or `critical`, every seat of a `reviewed` run (producer and each checker) must run on its own provider family; a pool without enough families refuses the seat with reason `independence`. `panel` keeps its soft spread.
- The `/fgOS:cook` slash command is now `/fgOS:deliver` (skill `plugins/fgOS/skills/deliver/`): same behavior, freeing the name `cook` for the orchestration skill planned next. `fgos-coding-driving` names it as a caller, and the shared coordination-driver fragment no longer teaches the removed `fgos coordination` verbs.
- `fgos run --resume` after a controller death no longer runs the agent again: the last attempt is taken through adopt and a settled result is used as it is (the unit carries on to commit, reviewer and summary). A `cancelled` or abandoned attempt is replaced by a new one that names it in `supersedesRunId`; an attempt still running is refused (`attempt-still-running`), and a second `--resume` of the same unit at the same time is refused (`resume-in-progress`). A unit never resumes on its own.
- `herdr-spawn` no longer runs a round loop in the controller. The seat goes through the same door as a headless one (attempt lock, envelope, supervisor), so a herdr seat cannot be started directly any more (`herdr-spawn-supervised-only`). On Windows, and where herdr is not usable, a pane attempt is refused with `terminal-mode-unsupported` and never changes to headless by itself; headless runs are unaffected.
- The confinement orphan reaper is gone. A private home belongs to its attempt and only adopt's finalize-home step removes it, while the attempt's lock is free and its process domain is empty; no sweep judges a home by a pid, a pane or an age any more. `fgos run` start, the runner loop start and `fgos doctor --fix` now only finish unfinished attempts. A herdr-spawn launch without a supervised attempt is refused (`attempt-required`), `fgos dispatch probe-account` no longer sweeps after closing panes, and the doctor check `confinement-orphaned-resources-reaped` now only tightens root modes, removes empty per-dispatch directories and `--fix` removes a home left by a dead dispatch outside the assignment door (judged by its pid alone, only on that explicit fix). Homes written by an older release with a pane binding are not reaped by this release: remove them with the previous release's `fgos run` before activating.
- The Git component spec (`fgos-git`, `docs/platform/git/spec.md`) is accepted: it is the single owner of every fgOS git mutation (commits, merges and land, worktrees, refs, fetch and push, and the publication of `refs/fgos/*` for the Event Store), and Workflow, Execution, Work, Event Store and setup become its consumers. No behavior changes yet; today's git writers stay until the Git plan replaces them.
- Doctor check `herdr-available` is replaced by `terminal-control`, which asks the terminal port instead of running `herdr --version` itself and keeps the `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` diagnosis. A machine without herdr now gets a warning, not a failure.
- A later step of one run whose earlier tab already closed itself opens a new tab with the same label instead of failing to find the old one.
- Windows: every terminal operation answers `unsupported` until herdr ships a Windows build; doctor says so, and direct (headless) mode is unaffected.
- `fgos unlock` is removed; the verb now answers `unknown verb "unlock"`, and the `/fgOS:unlock` command is gone. A held repo lock always has a live holder (kernel lock, no TTL, no stale record), so there is nothing to clear: wait, or stop a wedged holder with `fgos lock fence <name> [--param k=v] [--yes] [--attest-stopped]`. It lists the holders (pid, start time, command line), asks for confirmation, sends SIGTERM by identity, waits 5 s, sends SIGKILL, and checks with a probe that the lock is free; it never takes a lock from a live holder, and where holders cannot be listed `--attest-stopped` only re-checks. The skill `fgos-unlock` is now `fgos-lock-fence`.
- `fgos lock-status --json` reports every repo and machine lock of the registry as `free` or `held` (`locks`, with holder pids and the filesystem guarantee); the main checkout lock is under `mainCheckout` (`outcome` is `free` or `held`, `holders` replaces `holderPid`; `lockAge`, `remainingTtl` and `live`/`stale`/`ambiguous` are gone) and the commit-activity beacon moved from `activity` to `beacon`.
- `fgos main-checkout-reset` runs while holding the main checkout lock; with another process holding it the verb refuses at once with `lock-timeout`, naming the lock and the holder pid, and touches nothing. `fgos take`/`pick` wait for the main checkout lock as before (`--wait`, `--no-wait`).
- `.fgos/locks/*.lock` files never count as a change in an item's own footprint at `fgos return`.
- The main checkout lock, the merge slot of each target ref and the new `worktree-admin` lock (around every `git worktree add`) are kernel locks taken through one door (`src/runner/repo-locks.mjs`): no TTL, no ambiguous state, no recognition of a holder by pid, and a holder that dies releases at once. A git child of a checkpoint or merge, and the pre-commit hook it runs, act under the lock because they inherit the locked file description (`FGOS_LOCK_FD`); `FGOS_MAIN_LOCK_HOLDER_PID` is gone. A claim holds the main checkout lock through its `.fgos` checkpoint, worker-slot check and claim record, and creates its `--isolate` worktree after releasing it.
- `fgos doctor --fix` (with every fgOS process stopped) also fences the old main checkout lock and one old merge slot per local branch with a `TOMBSTONE` directory at `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` and `.fgos/merge-slot--<ref>.lock`. A release from before this change that meets one fails with `EISDIR`, and its pre-commit hook refuses a commit on the main checkout; rolling back to it is by hand: remove those `TOMBSTONE` directories. The `lock-holders` and `lock-fences` doctor checks now cover these locks; a branch created after the fences were placed needs `fgos doctor --fix` once more for its slot.
- The state store takes one hot mutex per clone, `state` (work events, claims and the state view, replacing `.fgos/events.lock` and `.fgos/runtime/claims.lock`) or `porting-events` (replacing `.fgos/porting/events.lock`), through `withStateTx`: the record is `.fgos/locks/<resource>.hot`, a dead holder is cleaned only under a kernel lock, and the wait is 5 s. A claim checks the worker-slot ceiling in the same transaction as the claim record and takes the main checkout lock only around the `.fgos` checkpoint commit. `FGOS_EVENTS_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` is gone.
- Starting a subprocess inside a state transaction, or taking a state mutex again while holding one, throws `exec-under-hot-lock` / `hot-lock-reentry` at once. On Windows a hot record is never cleaned (no dead-holder judge yet): a stuck one is cleared with `fgos lock fence state`.
- A record that does not parse, or whose holder cannot be judged, is never cleaned: the waiter times out with `lock-record-unreadable`, and a person who confirmed the holder is gone runs `fgos lock fence state` (or `porting-events`).
- `fgos doctor --fix` (with every fgOS process stopped) also fences the three old state locks with a `TOMBSTONE` directory at `.fgos/events.lock`, `.fgos/runtime/claims.lock` and `.fgos/porting/events.lock`. A release from before this change that reaches any of them stops with a raw `EISDIR` (measured with the real old `withEventsLock` and `withClaimsLock`).
- `runner.maxTier` no longer holds down a capability that declares a higher `rigor` itself in `runner.capabilities`: its seats run up to that rigor's tier (with the committed config, `architecture:synthesize`, `architecture:shape` and `architecture:explain` now run at `frontier`). A unit's rigor and a tier override still stop at `runner.maxTier`. `fgos doctor` check `capability-rigor-ceiling` lists the capabilities lifted this way and the model they run.
- Each agent family now has one executor. The `claude-herdr` executor is merged into `claude` (its pane invocation `claude-herdr-bwrap` moves there), and `glm-herdr` is removed (GLM runs headless through OpenRouter only). The 26 capabilities that named `claude-herdr` now name `claude`, so they run claude both inside herdr (in a pane) and headless; before, headless they fell over to codex, gemini or xai. Replace `--provider claude-herdr` with `--provider claude`.
- Agents now receive the full locked law list L1-L10 (L9 and L10 were missing from the projected instructions) and a new instruction unit, `core/instructions/design-principles.md`, with seven design principles (one door, bottom-up layering, thin drivers behind ports, Rust-first foundations, correctness first, KISS/DRY, one authority per decision). The coding worker contract and `fgos-coding-implement` now require searching the whole repository for an existing mechanism before adding a new one, importing the shared module an import guard names instead of copying code, and deleting the old path in the same change when replacing a mechanism.
- Every `fgos` verb now refuses a flag its registry entry does not declare: exit 4, `unknown flag "--x" for "fgos <verb>"` plus the verb's valid flags and a pointer to `--help`, instead of silently ignoring a typo that could make a command do something else. One check serves both doors: the legacy-node payload reads `src/cli/command-registry.mjs`, and the Rust host reads the same flag lists projected into `command-routes.json` (`accepted_flags` / `subcommand_flags`, regenerate with `node scripts/export-command-selectors.mjs`). `--dir`, `--json` and `--help` are accepted everywhere; the `--name=value` form is not accepted by the legacy-node verbs (write `--name value`). Flags the handlers already read but the registry never listed are now declared (for example `--worktree`, `--trust-dir`, `--no-timeout`, `--stance-options`, `--runtime-json`), so they show up in `fgos <verb> --help --json`.
- `fgctl init`, `upgrade` and `repair` decide on the main checkout only by probing its kernel lock; the old `.fgos/main-checkout.lock` file (a live pid, a session id, an unparseable record or a tombstone) is no longer read, and the `lock-ambiguous` and `lock-unsupported` refusals are gone.
- The `fgctl` activation lock, the machine install lock and the Observe store lock are kernel locks (`<fgosDir>/locks/activation.lock`, `<stateRoot>/locks/install.lock`, `<fgosDir>/locks/observe.lock`): no TTL, no stale reclaim, and a killed holder frees the lock at once, so there is no 3-minute activation or 30-second Observe expiry to wait out and no stuck `install.lock` to delete by hand (the Observe lock waits 5 s and writes its shard snapshot under the lock). `.fgos/installation/activation.lock`, `<stateRoot>/install.lock` and `.fgos/observe/.lock` become tombstone directories, so an older `fgctl` or `fgos` stops with an error there. `fgos doctor --fix` places those three fences only once the workspace's activated release is the one that takes them as kernel locks, so an older `fgctl` can still upgrade the workspace first. On Windows these locks work like elsewhere through the Windows lock driver.
- Gateway, sessions and runner locks are kernel locks in `.fgos/locks/`; a dead holder releases at once. An older release meets a `TOMBSTONE` directory at `.fgos/{gateway,sessions,runner}.lock` and fails with `EISDIR`.
- The full-suite queue is a machine-wide kernel lock at `~/.local/state/fgos/locks/full-suite.lock`, replacing the `/tmp` lock file and its stale-lock reclaim. Branches created before this change keep the old `/tmp` queue and do not queue with newer ones. `npm test` resolves the host binary first (`FGOS_HOST_BIN`, else it builds one with cargo) and then takes the queue; without a host binary it stops with `lock-driver-unavailable`, and `FGOS_FULL_SUITE_QUEUE=off` runs unqueued.
- The provider account locks and the provider-capacity state lock are kernel locks per machine (no longer per runtime directory); the generation directories no longer grow. An older release sees "held by pid 1" on these locks.
- The per-worktree dispatch lock is a kernel lock (still per `.fgos`), keyed by the directory's identity, so a worktree reached through a symlink is the same lock; a dead holder releases it at once and no orphaned `dispatch--*.lock` file blocks a resume any more. A live dispatcher that hangs keeps its worktree locked until it exits. `reconcile.lock` is a kernel lock at `.fgos/locks/reconcile.lock`, and `fgos dispatch reconcile clear-cwd-lock` now only reports whether the lock is held.
- The Rust host sets `FGOS_STATE_ROOT` for the Node payload, and dispatch pins it into every child, so a sandbox HOME does not move the state root. The npm package ships the lock registry `packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json`.
- Taking locks out of order inside one lock scope throws `lock-order-violation` at once. Each lock door takes its own scope today, so locks taken through different doors are not yet checked against each other.
- An older fgOS release run against a fenced workspace fails at its first lock (`EISDIR`, `lock-busy`, `already being advanced`, or a provider lock held by pid 1). Never delete a `TOMBSTONE` directory or a pid-1 generation by hand, unless rolling back to a release from before this one.
- Writer ids change, so settle or release every open claim with the old release before activating this one: `CODEX_THREAD_ID` now identifies a Codex pane (it ranks after `FGOS_SESSION_ID` and before `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`); a bare shell, agy, pi or omp pane resolves to its pane's root shell (the highest ancestor holding a terminal) instead of the herdr server or the CLI's own pid; a process with no terminal above it resolves to its session id.
- Every state write now needs the Rust host binary to name its writer: through the `fgos` command it is always there; `node bin/fgos.mjs` and the npm global `fgos` find it from the project's activation or `FGOS_HOST_BIN`, and otherwise stop with a clear `precondition` error instead of guessing. A commit at the main checkout between merging this change and activating it is refused with `host-version-mismatch` until the release is activated.
- Observe names writer shards (`.fgos/observe/<store>/<writer>.jsonl`) and friction `sessionId` from the same identity: a Claude or Codex session writes under its session id, and every command from one terminal pane shares `pid-<pane root>` instead of one shard per process.
- A runtime claim can now be released only by the writer that took it, the same rule a settle already follows. Another writer is refused with `releaseClaim: writer identity mismatch for "<id>" ...` and the claim stays in place; a parent or lineage id grants nothing. The stale-claim reclaim in `pick` and `fgos unclaim` still clear another session's dead or orphaned claim, and `fgos unclaim` output then carries `admin: {reason, ownerWriterId, releasedByWriterId}`.
- `fgos run` and `fgos workflow start|resume|answer --foreground` now exit with distinctive non-zero exit codes for non-pass outcomes (`policy-refusal`: 4, `provider-limit`: 10, `execution-failure`: 11, `partial-writes`: 12, `blocked`: 13, `findings`: 14; 0 on `pass`) while preserving the structured JSON envelope `fgos.v1` (RUL99). Read-only commands like `fgos workflow status` exit 0.
- `herdr-spawn` now defaults `promptDelivery` to `"inline"` (typing the full rendered brief directly into the pane via bracketed paste while still writing `brief-<round>.md` to disk with a recovery pointer), so a person watching the pane sees the task prompt in the TUI conversation; `"file-pointer"` remains supported per invocation or via `FGOS_HERDR_PROMPT_DELIVERY=file-pointer`. `confirmBriefSubmitted` now detects collapsed TUI paste chips (`[Pasted text #1 +N lines]`, `[paste #1 +N lines]`, `[Paste]`, `#1 … +N lines`, and OMP's `Pasted N lines` modal menu) in `promptText` and the bottom composer lines of the visible screen, `workerBaseEnv` and `SHELL_MANAGED_ENV` preserve the pane's own `TERM`/`HERDR_PANE_ID` and strip parent `OMPCODE`/`OMP_PROFILE`/`PI_PROFILE`/`PI_CONFIG_FILES`, and `executors.xai` gains the confined `omp-herdr-vantt` pane invocation.
